content.text: Spring Batch ItemWriters are used to write processed data to various destinations, including files, databases, XML, or JSON. Each writer is specialized for a particular type of output.
Used to write data into flat files (CSV, TXT, etc.).

items: Resource – Target file or location where the data will be written.
LineAggregator – Converts an object into a string format for writing.

content.text: Usage: Ideal for exporting processed data to CSV or other delimited text files.
Used to write data into JSON files.

items: JsonObjectMarshaller – Converts a Java object into a JSON string.

content.text: Usage: Useful when the output must be in JSON format, e.g., for REST API consumption or data interchange.
Used to write data into a relational database using JDBC.

items: SQL query – SQL statement for inserting or updating data.
ItemPreparedStatementSetter – Optional, used for mapping object fields to SQL parameters (if not using bean mapping).

content.text: Usage: Efficient for batch inserts or updates into a database. Suitable for medium to large datasets.

rows: Uses LineAggregator to map Object → String
Uses SQL + DataSource to insert/update records

items: StepScope: For writers that depend on job parameters (e.g., dynamic file names), use @StepScope to defer bean creation until the step starts.
Writers are usually part of a chunk-oriented step, paired with ItemReader and ItemProcessor.
Spring Batch also provides other writers for JPA (JpaItemWriter) and Hibernate (HibernateItemWriter) for ORM-based database operations.
